item.title: Tailoring Cathode Interphase with Cyclic Ethers toward Stable Lithium‐Metal Batteries
item.description:

ENERGY & ENVIRONMENTAL MATERIALS | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This work reveals that cyclic ether ring structure controls ring-opening thermodynamics and cathode interphase chemistry in lithium-metal batteries. Comparing DOL and DOX shows distinct interfacial pathways: DOL enables stable LiFePO₄ cycling, while DOX stabilizes high-voltage NCM811. The findings establish interfacial reactivity matching as a design principle for tailoring ether electrolytes, advancing durable lithium-metal batteries.

item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work shows that activating selenium anionic redox overcomes phase-selectivity limits in copper selenide cathodes, converting zincophobic CuSe into a high-capacity electrode (4 to 413 mAh g⁻¹, doubled voltage, 4000-cycle life). It enables the whole CuySe family as stable zinc-battery cathodes and generalizes to other nucleophilic additives, revitalizing a dormant material class.

item.title: Elucidating Polymer–Cathode Interfacial Interactions in Pyrolytic Pretreatment of Spent Lithium-Ion Batteries
item.description:

ACS Nano | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This study overturns the assumption that pyrolysis pretreatment is inert to spent battery cathodes. It reveals that carbonaceous residues from PVDF/separator interact with NCM surfaces, forming oxygen-rich coatings along grain boundaries that block lithium diffusion and cut recovery below 80%. Raising oxygen partial pressure removes these barriers, restoring 96.88% efficiency—highlighting pyrolysis's critical, previously overlooked role in recycling.
🏷 spent lithium-ion batteries · pyrolysis · cathode interface · PVDF · lithium recovery

It forms a MgF₂-rich bilayer SEI enabling stable cycling at 60–80°C with 35 mV overpotential. This resolves Mg–eutectic incompatibility, advancing high-temperature, flame-retardant magnesium batteries.
